metaData.originalTitle: Claude Code 工程负责人 Fiona Fung：如何打造全世界最 AI Native 的工程团队?
metaData.title: Fiona Fung, Engineering Lead at Claude Code: How to Build the Most AI-Native Engineering Team?
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Fiona Fung, head of Claude Code, shares how to build an AI-native engineering team: writing code is no longer the bottleneck; validation and measurement become core; hiring focuses on either product-oriented builders or deep system experts; management is automated through an always-on Claude session, emphasizing high agency paired with high accountability.
metaData.summary: This article is compiled from an in-depth interview with Fiona Fung on Lenny's Podcast. Fiona is the engineering lead for Claude Code and Cowork, with over 25 years of experience in leadership roles at companies including IBM, Microsoft (working on Visual Studio and TypeScript), and Meta (founding Facebook Marketplace, working on AR glasses). The article revolves around the core insight that "writing code is exiting the bottleneck position." Key themes discussed include: When designers and PMs can all submit code, validation replaces coding as the new bottleneck; teams should codify what "good" means into specifications stored in the repository, and let Claude verify against them; hiring is limited to two types—builders with product dreams and deep system experts who tackle tough problems, matched with the principle of "trust but verify"; management is being reshaped by asynchronous culture—a permanent Claude remote session is attached to all codebases, maintaining full awareness at all times. Routines go beyond cron jobs by having a "brain" that can autonomously generate prompts, dispatch agents, and produce reviewable PRs; high agency must be paired with high accountability—grant freedom while requiring clear validation hypotheses and responsible parties; managers must live in the product and practice dogfooding—when data and individual cases conflict, sometimes trust the case; the differentiator is a growth mindset, and what holds people back is fear—encourage doing things that scare you. The article also covers JIT (Just-in-Time) planning, role fusion for engineers, proactively managing quality with a "bad & sad" framework, and the culture of cutting useless processes. The compilation retains the essence of the original interview with added editor commentary, offering high value for engineering managers in the AI era.

mainPoints.point: Writing code is no longer the bottleneck; validation and measurement are the new bottlenecks.
mainPoints.explanation: When AI enables everyone to submit code, the constraint shifts from 'who writes' to 'how to verify.' Teams need to codify what 'good' means into repo specifications, let Claude automate verification, and be cautious not to mistake 'being busy' for 'making progress.'

mainPoints.point: Only hire two types: product-oriented builders and deep system experts.
mainPoints.explanation: One type can build end-to-end ideas into great products; the other guards deep areas like distributed systems that require rigorous oversight. The underlying principle is trust but verify.

mainPoints.point: High agency must be paired with high accountability.
mainPoints.explanation: Give everyone the freedom to act independently, but they must clearly state the validation hypotheses and who is responsible. Freedom and accountability are two sides of the same coin, especially critical for an AI-native team.

mainPoints.point: Managers must live in the product and practice dogfooding.
mainPoints.explanation: No dashboard can replace the feel of using the product firsthand; many critical judgments come from specific cases. When data and individual cases conflict, sometimes trust the case.

mainPoints.point: The differentiator is a growth mindset; what holds people back is fear.
mainPoints.explanation: What made you successful in the past may not carry you forward. When facing fear, first ask what's within your control, then go do the scary thing.

keyQuotes: What made you successful in the past may not carry you forward.
If you weren't afraid, what would you do? From time to time, do something that scares you.
Where users take detours is the next product opportunity.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Is Not the Goal, Knowledge Is the Moat — Knowledge Accumulation Practices of an AI Engineering Delivery Team
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on the engineering delivery practices of an AI Team, this article proposes that knowledge accumulation is more important than workflow orchestration, and systematically introduces a complete methodology encompassing a five-layer knowledge storage architecture, a three-level maturity system, and how workflows serve knowledge accumulation.

relatedArticles.title: Understanding Hermes in One Article: How the New Top-Tier Agent Self-Evolves from Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth analysis of the core innovation of the Hermes Agent—the Skills closed-loop system—detailing its complete implementation mechanism, from experience extraction and knowledge storage to intelligent retrieval and self-improvement, along with its engineering trade-offs and security considerations.

relatedArticles.title: Investing 10,000 RMB in AI: A Year of Tools, Practices, and Reflections
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: A systematic summary of a veteran developer's practical experience in the AI wave, covering everything from MAC toolchain optimization and Harness Engineering architectural constraints to building an Agent-driven automated learning loop.

relatedArticles.title: Harness Engineering: How I Spent a Week Boosting AI Coding Rate to 90% in an Enterprise App
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically introduces Harness Engineering, a new AI coding paradigm that elevates the AI code rate of an enterprise Java application from 25% to over 90% by building a four-element system of rules, skills, knowledge, and change management.

relatedArticles.title: The Super Individual | To The Crazy Ones
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article delves into the essence of the 'Super Individual,' arguing it is not a result of skill training but a fundamental personality structure driven by curiosity, and suggests that large companies should inspire rather than cultivate such individuals by providing complete closed loops.

relatedArticles.title: Which Path Leads to the Final Destination of the 'World Model'? | A Conversation with Huang Biwei: Founder of Aether AI
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Professor Huang Biwei, founder of Aether AI, deeply elaborates on the technical path of the 'Causal World Model,' compares mainstream approaches such as video generation, VLA, and WAM, and argues that causal AI is the only way to reach the final destination of embodied intelligence.

relatedArticles.title: “Is AGI Here? I Used It for a Week and My Scalp Tingled” | A Conversation with Zhang Haoran: Co-founder of Moxt
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Through an in-depth interview with Moxt co-founder Zhang Haoran, this article explores how AI Native Workspaces are reshaping file systems and collaboration models to evolve organizations from 'human-computer interaction' to 'AI team collaboration.'

relatedArticles.title: What Are We Really Discussing When We Talk About Harness? | In-Depth Dialogue: MiniMax × Hermes Agent
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article compiles an in-depth dialogue hosted by Crossroads, featuring the MiniMax Agent team and the head of Hermes Agent. It delves into the core topics surrounding the shift in hype from OpenClaw to Hermes, exploring the definitions of Agent and Harness, multi-agent collaboration, self-evolution, the gap between Chinese and US models, and entrepreneurial opportunities in Agent Infra.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: 2026: The End of Software, the Fall of Engineers, the Disappearance of Mediocrity
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Using the sharp decline in US software stocks in early 2026 as a starting point, this article deeply analyzes how AI Agents are eroding the SaaS middle-layer business model, and explores structural shifts in software form from product to medium, and the engineer's role from writing code to understanding systems.
